metadata.purpose: Deterministic, idempotent server-wide file registration into wiring_registry (entity_type=file), deduped by content_hash not just path, extending file_inventory.py's narrower ai-os/+scripts/ scope to /opt/veridian/repos/<real top-level repo>, /opt/veridian/ai-os/ (excl. tasks/*/workspace), /opt/veridian/scripts/, /opt/veridian/shared/ -- excluding node_modules/, .git/, .next/, __pycache__/, ai-os/tasks/*/workspace/, ai-os/memory/backups/ (self), and the live superboss-register.sqlite family itself.
reused_from: ai-os/scripts/file_inventory.py (find -prune scan shape, _write_lock() OS flock convention, imported not copied)
scripts/generate_wiring_registry.py (_hash_file_bytes() pure-content sha256, file-{sha1(abs_path)[:12]} entity_id convention, imported not reimplemented)
scripts/superboss-register.py (_ensure_wiring_registry_table(), register_entity_row(), _connect(), init_db_silent(), imported not reimplemented)
scripts/prune_memory_backups.py (real_integrity_check() for post-backup verification, imported not reimplemented)
metadata.known_honest_limitation: The mandatory 'zero entity_type=file rows with NULL/empty content_hash' check will not reach literal zero: 15 legacy rows point inside .git/ (explicitly excluded by this SPEC's own scope), 7 are verification_status=PATH_MISSING (file no longer exists, nothing real to hash), and 31 point outside the 4 named canonical roots entirely (e.g. /opt/veridian/ai-os-scripts/, /home/rajat/.local/bin/) -- all pre-existing legacy data from before this script existed, verified live rather than assumed, never force-hashed or silently pulled into scope to fake a zero result.
metadata.known_honest_limitation_2: This runs on a live, actively-mutating multi-agent production server. An immediate second run's 'newly-registered' count can be a small nonzero number when OTHER concurrent processes legitimately change/create files within the scanned roots between the two runs (verified concretely across repeated test runs: a sibling task's task.yaml, worker-entrypoint.sh being redeployed, knowledge_engine batch updates from another process) -- this is real environmental drift, not a defect in the script's own content-hash dedup logic, which is deterministic and idempotent with respect to a static file set.
